title: Finding the Al G. Barnes Circus in Billboard
summary: Recovering in hospital, Joe finds an Al G. Barnes Circus ad in Billboard and wires trombonist Jug Everly to join in Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So I'm looking through there, and I wanted to see the routes of the different circuses. And this was about the middle of the summer. Hell, I can't remember what year it was...
Well, was Prohibition still on then?
So it must have been sometime...

Oh, yeah, Prohibition was on... This was in 1925! Because I didn't stay on that medicine show too long. It had to be '25... Yeah. Because I remember when I got to New Orleans, the World Series was on, the 1925 World Series, the Yankees and somebody... [SIC: In 1925, the Washington Senators played the Pittsburgh Pirates. So maybe it was 1926.]

Anyway, I seen in a Billboard the Al G. Barnes Circus was looking for musicians. They was playing in Cincinnati. So it just happened I knew one of the guys that had been on the Al G. Barnes Circus named Jug Everly, a trombone player out of Los Angeles here. So I sent him a telegram. And he said, sure he could use me; join the circus in Cincinnati.
Was he the director of the band, or what?
